newsitem.title: USA: Bank of Boston closing 65 Mass. branches.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Boston closing 65 Mass. branches.

text.p: Bank of Boston Corp. will close 65 Massachusetts bank branches, affecting some 225,000 customers in a cost-cutting move stemming from its purchase of BayBanks Inc., the company announced Friday.
Bank of Boston said it expected the affected branches' 400 employees would have jobs elsewhere in the company.
The closings, expected to be completed by midyear, will leave 356 Bank of Boston and BayBank branches around the state, the Boston-based bank holding company said.
Bank of Boston said the remaining branches will take the new name BankBoston by mid-1997.

The closings will leave branches in 50 of the 51 cities or towns affected. Only the small town of Carlisle in northeastern Massachusetts will be left without a branch, and Bank of Boston said it was leaving an automated teller machine there.
Bank of Boston and BayBank have some 2 million customers in Massachusetts.

Bank of Boston announced in December 1995 that it was acquiring BayBanks to create a $62 billion company. When the merger was completed last July, the new company pledged to save $230 million, partly by consolidating overlapping bank branches.
The company has already shed 16 BayBank branches and four Bank of Boston branches, selling them to U.S. Trust Corp. to comply with a Justice Department order regarding the merger.
The branches affected by Friday's announcement include three each in New Bedford and Springfield and one each in Boston, Cambridge and Worcester.
